articles.title: The Aegon’s Conquest Movie Needs to Look to Dune, Not Game of Thrones
articles.summary: To succeed as a feature film, Warner Bros.’ Aegon's Conquest needs to lean into the cinematic storytelling of the Dune movie trilogy rather than the formula of Game of Thrones.
articles.body:
Occasional vague book spoilers follow for Dune Messiah and Fire & Blood.

Despite social media’s insistence on spreading (likely false) casting rumors about it, all we know for certain about Warner Bros’ first Game of Thrones feature film is that it chronicles the story of Aegon’s Conquest, it’s being adapted from George R.R. Martin’s Targaryen history book Fire & Blood by House of Cards writer Beau Willimon , and it will be released in theaters sometime after 2027 .

Both House of the Dragon and A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms will likely have concluded their respective runs on HBO by the time Game of Thrones: Aegon’s Conquest hits cinemas near the end of this decade.

While a lot can happen in that time, let’s say everything remains on track and Warner Bros. does indeed produce an Aegon’s Conquest film in the next few years. It’s my opinion that the studio should look to one of its more recent film franchises as a template, rather than to its television predecessor, Game of Thrones , for how to bring Aegon’s Conquest to the big screen.

If they’re going to try to bring the story of a ruthless, seemingly invincible conqueror to theaters as a mainstream movie experience, then Warner Bros. should borrow from its own playbook in how it successfully adapted the complicated story of Dune for the silver screen. There are more parallels between the two sagas than one might initially expect.

The first step Warner Bros. should take is one they’ve successfully employed before with their top franchises and hire a visionary filmmaker to direct Aegon’s Conquest. Just as they recruited Christopher Nolan for the Dark Knight trilogy and Denis Villeneuve for Dune (and Warners-owned New Line Cinema signed Peter Jackson for Lord of the Rings), Warner Bros. would be in safe hands finding a strong filmmaker with a unique vision to ensure Aegon’s Conquest works as a feature film.

The studio must also decide if Aegon’s Conquest is a single (likely three-hour) film, a two-parter, or a trilogy. Any of those options could work but my gut says a two-part film would be ideal.

The Great Dictator: When Your Hero’s Really a Villain

Even if you haven’t read Frank Herbert’s books , the Dune movies have now made it clear that Paul Atreides is ultimately not your standard hero. The end of Dune: Part 2 saw Paul become the emperor and launch an intergalactic war. The upcoming Dune: Part 3 will depict the bitter price Paul and the universe pay for him to fulfill his destiny. Herbert never intended Paul to be deemed a hero; in fact, the story of Paul Atreides was designed to be a cautionary tale about the devastating sway charismatic political figures can have over their people.

George R.R. Martin ’s take on Aegon the Conqueror is, to me, less defined and judgmental than Herbert’s portrayal of Paul Atreides. In Fire & Blood, Martin chronicles the dragon-riding Targaryen dynasty, including the Dance of the Dragons civil war depicted in House of the Dragon. Historical details can be contradictory, and characters are often not much more than thumbnail sketches. House of the Dragon showrunner Ryan Condal has faced his fair share of backlash, including from Martin himself , for the choices he made in adapting the material for TV ( “It’s not TV. It’s HBO.” ). But choices had to be made since the source material itself, while at least complete, is not rich in character development.

Like Dune’s Paul Atreides, Aegon I Targaryen is responsible for countless deaths in his quest to become the sole ruler of his realm. The Targaryens arrived in Westeros following the Doom of Valyria , settling on the island of Dragonstone . By the time Aegon reached adulthood, he made it his mission to unite the long-warring Seven Kingdoms under the rule of one man: himself.

Both Dune and House of the Dragon/Game of Thrones have used prophecy as a means to explain the despotic actions of their antiheroic protagonists. Just as Paul Atreides cites his visions as justification for his holy war, so too will Aegon’s vision of a great looming terror in the North convince him that, as bloody as things get, his cause is just. (It should be noted that Martin’s novels have yet to include Aegon’s prophecy but the author told Condal that Aegon knew about the White Walkers .) For both Paul and Aegon, their adherence to prophecy makes them believe the ends justify the means, but they each lose their humanity and those they love most in the process.

Many Characters, But Make Sure It’s One Person’s Story

It’s tough to make a movie where an audience roots for a conqueror. Epics about Alexander the Great and Genghis Khan were notorious box office flops, while the exploits of William the Conqueror have largely been relegated to TV miniseries. But the Dune movies have so far managed to tell a grand story about a not terribly sympathetic protagonist and make audiences care about what happens next. That’s a big screen template Warner Bros. would be foolish not to revisit when adapting Aegon’s Conquest.

The first step there is accepting the inherent complexity and moral darkness of the central character and fully committing to exploring their descent into tyranny. And while the Dune movies contain intriguing supporting characters, the trilogy is ultimately Paul’s story. Similarly, Aegon’s Conquest needs to develop a small host of key supporting characters to illuminate the title character’s arc, but the filmmakers must make sure the focus remains on Aegon himself and his emotional and moral journey.

Dune’s supporting characters aid in humanizing Paul, particularly the tragic love story between Paul and Chani. Likewise, Martin’s source material offers screenwriter Beau Willimon two key supporting players who can illuminate the cost of Aegon’s ambition: his sister-wives Visenya and Rhaenys.

Without getting into too many book spoilers, Visenya and Rhaenys are key figures in helping Aegon conquer Westeros. Visenya is a steely warrior, while the younger Rhaenys is more playful and artsy. All three siblings fly fearsome dragons: Aegon rides Balerion the Black Dread , Visenya rides Vhagar (yes, the same giant beast flown by Aemond in House of the Dragon ), and Rhaenys flies Meraxes.

Just as Paul’s tragic falling out with Chani is gearing up to be a heartbreaker in Dune: Part 3 , whatever fates befall Aegon’s sister-wives during his conquest could weigh heavily on him, imbuing the conqueror with a vulnerability and pain he might not otherwise be willing to reveal.

Every Dragon in Game of Thrones: House of the Dragon

The Targaryens of this time had three dragons, an advantage that meant that, despite some of his opponents raising giant armies, they were ultimately no match against the power of these fire-breathing beasts. Soon, all the kingdoms except Dorne (more on them later) bent the knee to Aegon, and he became the first Targaryen king to rule Westeros.

Fire & Blood is a lot of “then this happened, then that happened” plotting where Aegon and the dragons wipe out one enemy kingdom after another. That could quickly prove tiresome and feel like an endless array of CGI mayhem that leaves little emotional impact on the viewer.

The filmmakers then should be selective in which battles they depict at length. A montage or simply seeing the aftermath of a battle could work just as well if the filmmakers aren’t planning on developing the vanquished much beyond getting them burned to a crisp by a dragon. The Dune movies have been judicious in when they showed the sandworms ; Aegon’s Conquest should be similarly choosy when it comes to dragon action scenes lest they become overkill.

The first two Dune movies pitted Paul and his allies against one distinct enemy: House Harkonnen . Aegon’s Conquest sees the title character battle a slew of kingdoms but, frankly, after a while it becomes repetitive seeing the same series of events play out but with different kingdoms (a king refuses to yield, dragons kill everybody, Aegon wins, wash, rinse, repeat).

There are two nemeses, though, that could fit the Harkonnen bill in Aegon’s Conquest. The first is King Harren the Black of House Hoare, the wicked lord of Harrenhal . Harren is a vicious, cruel man who built his giant castle using forced labor, shedding so much blood in its construction that Harrenhal is believed to be haunted. Harren the Black has all the odiousness and viciousness of a Baron Harkonnen that make him a fitting villain for Aegon to battle (and one player viewers wouldn’t mind seeing taken off the board in gory fashion).

House of the Dragon Season 3 directly tied itself to Harren the Black through the character of Alys Rivers (perhaps we’ll even see actress Gayle Rankin appear in Aegon’s Conquest), and the castle’s infamous destruction should make for a grand, devastating set-piece in the film.

A second worthy adversary for Aegon and his sisters to face is Meria Martell, the princess of Dorne. She shares the same hideous, corpulent physicality as Baron Harkonnen or Jabba the Hutt, but Meria’s keen military mind and cunning make her a foe worthy of admiration. Meria and Dorne’s resistance against Aegon the Conqueror was notably recalled by Ormund Hightower to Daeron Targaryen in House of the Dragon Season 3, Episode 5.

Meria’s shadowy tactics could mirror the Fremen ’s guerrilla campaign against the Harkonnens on Arrakis. Since we all know Dorne never bent the knee, this defeat – and what Aegon will lose personally in his quest to subdue Dorne – could prove the thematic culmination of Aegon’s arc. He achieves his conquest but, like Paul Atreides, it costs him everything he loves

While we’re still a few years away from Game of Thrones: Aegon’s Conquest hitting theaters, it would be wise for Warner Bros. to see its recent franchise success with the similarly dark and complex Dune saga as a roadmap in how to bring Westeros to the big screen.

articles.title: No Rest For The Wicked 1.0 Launch Delayed to March 2027
articles.summary: No Rest for the Wicked developer Moon Studios has delayed the game's long-awaited 1.0 launch until March 2027.
articles.body:
No Rest for the Wicked developer Moon Studios has delayed the game's long-awaited 1.0 launch until March 2027.

The news was confirmed today alongside a fresh trailer for the game, and an explanation that the wait would bring improved gameplay performance, a tightened class system and further polish to make the action RPG finally hit version 1.0 at "the standard it deserves."

If it feels like we've been waiting a long time for No Rest for the Wicked version 1.0, then that's because its initial PC early access build arrived back in April 2024. When the game does hit 1.0 in March 2027, it will do so for PlayStation 5 and PC. Nintendo Switch 2 and Xbox Series X/S versions are still planned, but lack a formal launch date.

As a reward for players' patience, the game's Founders Pack of extra in-game items has been extended to anyone who purchases the game before January 1, 2027, with recent purchases now retroactively included in the offer. That's for PC players, to be clear, while PS5 pre-order customers will get a similar offer early next year.

"Let me apologize," said Moon Studios' Thomas Mahler in a video published today. "I hope you folks understand that this is huge passion project of ours. We have been working on the first prototypes for No Rest of the Wicked since 2016. We'd just like to take this extra time to make sure that we land this plane safely and that we don't ship with any silly little bugs left."

Mahler previously blamed the lesser-powered Xbox Series S for the game's Xbox Series version taking longer to launch.

articles.title: Project Hail Mary Is Getting a VR Game This Fall
articles.summary: A new chapter from the world of Project Hail Mary is being released as a VR game this fall.
articles.body:
A new chapter from the world of Project Hail Mary is being released as a VR game this fall.

Developer Maze Theory is producing a new VR/mixed reality title known as Project Hail Mary: Journey Among the Stars, which will tell an original new story in the sci-fi world. Players will step into the shoes of Ryland Grace (who appears to be a silent protagonist this time around) and work together with Rocky to diagnose and solve problems on your ship. It's unclear how long this game will be or how expansive it is, but it looks like a fun way for fans to get more Project Hail Mary content (and more Rocky).

The game will see actor James Ortiz reprising his role as the voice of Rocky, who expressed a lot of excitement in returning to the character for this game.

“Playing Rocky again for the game has been really special," said Ortiz. "Fans will be able to step inside the world of Project Hail Mary, interact with Rocky using the same character model from the film, and experience a completely new part of his journey with Grace. It is as close as you can get to the cinematic experience, but this time you are inside it.”

Project Hail Mary is one of the breakout successes from Hollywood this year, proving people are hungry for well-made original films. The movie grossed $684 million at the box office and became a viral sensation on platforms like TikTok. Although there's nothing officially in the works as far as we know, a sequel is on the table and likely in demand from Amazon . However, it falls on author Andy Weir to produce one, and it's unclear if that will happen or what it would even look like.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: New American Horror Story 13 Poster and Plot Teases Revealed
articles.summary: Ryan Murphy's dark and disturbing series - drops a new poster, episode titles and short synopses for installments 4-6.
articles.body:
Someone over at Hulu decided to lock in on the social media campaign for American Horror Story 13 — the latest in Ryan Murphy's dark and disturbing series — dropping a new poster, episode titles and short synopses for installments 4–6.

The poster is classic Murphy, featuring a figure in a full black latex gimp suit, brandishing a giant black sunflower. Several characters have rocked the outfit — also known as the Rubber Man costume — throughout previous seasons, most notably Tate Langdon (played by Evan Peters in American Horror Story: Murder House).

That makes sense, as Murphy told Vogue that 13 would see some of the show's most popular characters return. "I just thought the number 13 was infused with so much stuff in the horror genre, and I wanted to do a greatest hits season," Murphy said.

Meanwhile, the plot teases for each are a sexy ankle flash of the horrible delights that await in episodes 4–6.

American Horror Story 13 will premiere just in time for spooky season, on FX on September 24, 2026.

She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. articles.title: New Christmas LEGO Sets Announced, Including Buddy the Elf
articles.summary: LEGO is releasing brand new Christmas sets for 2026 this October, including Buddy the Elf, an Up-Scaled Mrs. Claus Minifigure, and a Santa’s Holiday Countdown build.
articles.body:
Christmas may be a few months away, but LEGO isn't waiting until then to drop some exciting new seasonally-appropriate sets for builders. The company has just announced five new sets that are perfect for the holidays releasing soon on October 1: Buddy the Elf (from the classic 2003 holiday movie, Elf ), a Santa’s Holiday Countdown set, an Up-Scaled Mrs. Claus Minifigure , and more.

For those who can't wait to get in the Christmas spirit this year, preorders are live at the LEGO store for Buddy, priced at $39.99, and Santa's Holiday Countdown, priced at $59.99. Unfortunately, the big Mrs. Claus minifigure, which is also listed for $59.99, is not up for preorder right now but will be available to buy on October 1.

Santa's Holiday Sleigh Adventure (40866)

Head to the links below to secure a set for the season, and learn a little more about each build.

This delightful Buddy the Elf build looks like a must for those who adore the Will Ferrell-led holiday flick. Recommended for ages 12 and up, this build features 713 bricks that piece together to form Buddy and his arctic puffin friend.

Of course, there's also candy canes around the snowy base and a maple syrup bottle. Can't forget two of the most important food groups.

The Santa's Holiday Countdown set looks like such a fun build for those looking to keep track of the days leading up to Christmas.

With 873 pieces, and recommended for those aged 10 and up, you'll create Santa Claus coming down a chimney with a little countdown clock on it. With the help of knobs on the side of the set, you can turn the countdown blocks on the chimney to see how much time is left until the big day.

Last October saw the release of LEGO's big Up-Scaled Santa Minifigure, and this year Mrs. Claus will be making an appearance in the same format. Her 904-piece build features a posable head, arms, and hands, and similar to the Santa's Holiday Countdown set above, is also recommended for ages 10 and up.

These new LEGO sets are just a few of the company's new releases, and there's plenty more to come in the months ahead alongside them. If you're curious what else is dropping soon, it's always worth having a look at our rundown of all of September's new LEGO sets , as well as every upcoming LEGO set announced so far.

articles.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Beta Extended

articles.body:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 developer Infinity Ward has announced that the playable beta for the next first-person shooter in the long-running franchise has been extended until 10pm PT tonight/1am ET tomorrow morning.

"A little more time on the clock," the studio posted on its X account. We see you grinding out those Beta Rewards and camos, so we’re giving you some extra time. The #MW4 Open Beta is extended until 10 PM PT tonight. 2XP + Double Weapon XP stay active until close. Enjoy!"

Infinity Ward has already updated the beta, most recently to address TTK criticisms and tweak the weapons, but they also pushed changes out to beta testers last week as well.

It's been an unusual beta this year in the sense that a fan-favorite character's haircut has been the subject of some controversy , and the beta also included a single-player mission for the first time ever.

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is due out on October 23 (although for those that preorder, you'll get access to the campaign on October 16) for PS5, Xbox Series X|S, PC, and Nintendo Switch 2, though it won't be included in Xbox Game Pass Ultimate on day one this year.

articles.title: Tomb Raider Series Broke UK Crew Safety Laws, Report Confirms, Months After Star Sophie Turner Injured in Separate Incident
articles.summary: Amazon MGM Studios' new Tomb Raider series broke health and safety laws during production, just months after filming had to be halted due to star Sophie Turner's on-set injury.
articles.body:
Amazon MGM Studios' new Tomb Raider series broke UK health and safety laws during production, it's emerged, just months after filming had to be halted due to star Sophie Turner sustaining an injury on set.

In a separate incident, the production was found to have failed its "biological monitoring" duties regarding the use of potentially hazardous chemicals — isocyanate paints, which can cause asthma attacks.

Isocyanate paints require appropriate equipment to be worn during use and must be handled by properly protected staff, with the air then given up to 20 minutes to clear afterwards. Deadline reports that this was not adhered to on the Tomb Raider set, and the UK's Heath and Safety Executive (HSE) was forced to intervene.

The production was later confirmed to have broken the Health and Safety At Work Act 1974 and Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations 2002. Despite the UK's non-stop use as a filming destination, just four HSE interventions have taken place over the past four years, making this a noteworthy occurrence — particularly for such a high-profile series.

Earlier this year, an on-set injury forced the entire production to be suspended for two weeks while Turner underwent treatment . The former Game of Thrones star is understood to have suffered a back injury, though healed sooner than some had feared. Meanwhile, the show's crew was reportedly paid for the time spent on hiatus.

Filming for Turner's Tomb Raider series initially began in January , with a starry cast that includes British acting legend Celia Imrie, Harry Potter star Jason Isaacs, as well as Alien and Avatar icon Sigourney Weaver. One unannounced cast member has also been spotted filming — former Lara Croft voice actress Keeley Hawes, who many fans suspect will play Lara's mother Amelia, in a neat passing of the torch from the video game series.

Tomb Raider is set to be released on Prime Video, though currently lacks a release date.

articles.title: Godzilla Dev Wants to Do More Remasters, But 'a Lot of Conversations' Need to Happen First
articles.summary: Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered is the only remaster Pipeworks can confirm for now, but "a lot of stuff is on the table," and there are "a lot of conversations to be had" in the future.
articles.body:
Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered is the only remaster Pipeworks can confirm for now, but "a lot of stuff is on the table," and there are "a lot of conversations to be had" in the future.

The developer behind the November upgrade and the 2002 game it's based on opened up about the potential for more games in the series during an all-encompassing interview with IGN. With Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee officially coming back, the natural question we and everyone else had is: Will we be getting remasters for Godzilla: Save the Earth and Godzilla: Unleashed ?

According to senior designer Simon Strange, it's too soon to say, but that doesn't mean he isn't rooting for it to happen.

"Let me tell you, I had that desire long before we announced this game, so I get it," Strange said. "I want to do all that stuff, too. I mean, all that stuff is now technically possible."

Strange said a Pipeworks engineer recently created a tool that allowed them to bring old assets out of their original Spigot engine and into Unreal, thus resulting in Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered. He confirmed the same technology could be used to create upgraded re-releases for the rest of the studio's arena fighter trilogy, too. Unfortunately, the studio hasn't signed any relevant contracts with publisher Atari just yet.

When Pipeworks launched its original Godzilla game for GameCube in 2002, the team only consisted of about "12 people in one room." The company has since ballooned to include around 300 people who are often spread across dozens of different projects at any given time. That includes more focused games like Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered, as well as titles it's served as co-developer on, like Marathon, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3, Concord, and Destiny 2.

Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered Screenshots

Choosing how to allocate those resources isn't simple, and whether the demand for more Godzilla remasters is even there remains to be seen. Atari and Pipeworks have nothing to announce, even if Strange loves "the idea of bringing all that content back to the players." The one catch, though, is that if more remasters do come to be, it would take a little more than a new coat of paint to get Godzilla: Unleashed into shape.

"I would especially love – and I'm speaking a little out of turn here – but I would love to avenge the sort of mediocre release of Godzilla: Unleashed," Strange said. "There was a lot of trouble on that, and I had a conversation where we were like, 'Would we remaster every possible game?' I was like, 'Nobody wants a straightforward remaster of Godzilla: Unleashed because that game was busted in some ways.' So, if we wanted to revisit that content, I'd want to do it better."

Strange isn't exactly wrong; the third entry in Pipeworks' arena brawler trilogy isn't viewed quite as fondly as the others. Godzilla: Unleashed has a "Generally Unfavorable" score of 44 on review website Metacritic , with IGN's review giving it a 4.9/10 . For reference, Destroy All Monsters Melee has a 73 on the site (IGN: 8.5/10 ), while Save the Earth has a 63 (IGN: 6.5/10 ).

Again, nothing is officially in the works yet, but should more remaster plans materialize, it sounds like handling one project might be a bit easier than the other. We'll hopefully have a better idea of what the future holds when Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered launches November 3, 2026, for PC via Steam, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S.

"We've got a whole biz dev section, Atari's got a whole biz dev section, they're talking based on the response… I mean, a lot of stuff is on the table," Strange added. "There's a lot of conversations to be had in the future, and I'm very excited for all of that."

Strange also teased that he considers Pipeworks' November video game to be 40% remaster and 60% new, but you'll have to wait to read IGN's full interview to learn more on that front. We'll share the rest of the conversation soon, but until then, be sure to check out our preview . You can also see what Strange had to say about the battle between his game and Grand Theft Auto 6 .

articles.title: Preorders Have Dropped for Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender’s 4K Steelbook, Out Next February
articles.summary: Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender is getting a 4K steelbook release on February 9, 2027. Here's where you can preorder a copy before then.
articles.body:
Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender is among our best reviewed movies of the year so far, with our review by Alex Zalben calling it "a lovingly crafted and gorgeously animated movie that features a welcome return for Team Avatar." If you're someone who agrees with that, and have been itching to get a physical copy of it, today is your lucky day.

Preorders are officially live for Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender's 4K steelbook at select retailers for $45.99 ( see it here at Amazon ). Unfortunately, there's quite a long wait until it's out on February 9 next year, but don't wait until then to grab it. Steelbook stock can disappear fast, so now is the time to pick it up before that happens.

Preorder Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender 4K Steelbook

Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender - Steelbook (4K UHD + Digital))

As of the time of this writing, this 4K steelbook only seems to be available at Amazon, but that will likely change with time. Once more retailers have it, we'll be sure to include them here.

Similarly, bonus features for this 4K steelbook haven't been announced yet. But again, when that changes, we'll mention them here.

If you're curious about our thoughts on the film, Zalben's 8/10 review of it highlighted that it's "big, bold, and stunningly animated with gorgeous imagery and huge fight scenes that were clearly crafted for the big screen." With that in mind, a 4K copy is sure to really shine on your screen at home if you adored the film.

While this 4K steelbook copy of Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender won't be out for quite some time, there's plenty more physical releases coming out in the months ahead to check out in the meantime. Our breakdown of upcoming 4Ks and Blu-rays can show you the highlights of what's still to come throughout the rest of this year, if you're looking to add more to your movie library.

articles.title: 15 Studio Ghibli Movies Are Getting Blu-ray Steelbook Reprints – Preorders Are Live
articles.body:
The Studio Ghibli animated films have been released a number of times on physical media. The most recent Blu-ray release came in brightly colored limited-edition steelbooks. Most of those have sold out widely – which is undoubtedly why they’re getting reprinted. The whole batch of 15 Ghibli films is up for preorder once again, set to release September 29.

We’re talking movies like Spirited Away, My Neighbor Totoro, Princess Mononoke, and most of the rest of the studio’s output over the past 40 years. Many of these are straight-up masterpieces of animation. So if you’ve been eager to add some of these to your collection, now is a good time to do so.

Preorder the Studio Ghibli Limited-Edition Reprints

Spirited Away: Limited Edition Steelbook

My Neighbor Totoro: Limited Edition Steelbook

Princess Mononoke: Limited Edition Steelbook

Kiki's Delivery Service: Limited Edition Steelbook

Howl's Moving Castle: Limited Edition Steelbook

Grave Of The Fireflies: Limited Edition Steelbook

Nausicaä Of The Valley Of The Wind: Limited Edition

From Up On Poppy Hill: Limited Edition Steelbook

When Marnie Was There: Limited Edition Steelbook

The Wind Rises: Limited Edition Steelbook

The Tale Of The Princess Kaguya: Limited Edition Steelbook

The Secret World Of Arrietty: Limited Edition Steelbook

Only Yesterday: Limited Edition Steelbook

I did some searching for the previous releases of these movies and found that two of them have not, in fact, sold out at Amazon. They’re available now, at lower prices. Feel free to pick these up, without having to wait for late September.

Kiki’s Delivery Service - $18.89 (available now)

Grave of the Fireflies - $26.99 (available now)

Most of these movies were written and directed by either Hayao Miyazaki or Isao Takahata. They’re all gorgeous to look at and sport high-caliber English voice work, with names like Cate Blanchett, Christian Bale, Edward James Olmos, Emily Blunt, Cary Elwes, Gillian Anderson, Jamie Lee Curtis, Amy Poehler, Dev Patel, Daisy Ridley, Hailee Steinfeld, Kiernan Shipka, and more showing up in the credits.

I’ve only seen a handful of these movies, but they were all at least good , and most of them were spectacular. My Neighbor Totoro is about a pair of kids with a neglectful — er, busy — dad who move to a new house and discover strange creatures that live in or near the house. Spirited Away is a gentle nightmare of a film, about a girl whose parents transform into pigs and she gets lost in a town filled with strange people and beasts.

So if you could use some high quality animation in your life, these Blu-ray steelbook editions would make a great addition to your collection.

Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's board game and LEGO coverage. You can follow him on Bluesky .

articles.title: Resident Evil Movie Popcorn Bucket Is an Organ Transplant Bag
articles.summary: The official new Resident Evil movie popcorn bucket is styled to look like an organ transplant bag, marking one of the horror franchise's most unsettling collectibles.
articles.body:
The popcorn bucket for director Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil movie has been revealed and it’s in the form of an organ transplant bag.

Exhibitors AMC Theaters and Regal Cinemas both posted images of the popcorn bucket, er, bag to their respective social media feeds Tuesday when announcing that tickets are now on sale for the video game movie adaptation.

“One Job: Deliver the Popcorn! See RESIDENT EVIL and purchase our concession collectible starting 9/17, available in theatres only while supplies last,” AMC wrote.

Not to be outdone, Regal posted: “Need a transplant? We recommend this popcorn bag 🫀🍿 Get your hands on the Resident Evil Organ Transplant Popcorn Bag when you see Resident Evil at Regal.”

One Job: Deliver the Popcorn! See RESIDENT EVIL and purchase our concession collectible starting 9/17, available in theatres only while supplies last. Get tickets: pic.twitter.com/Pvef8AK3H4

Need a transplant? We recommend this popcorn bag 🫀🍿 Get your hands on the Resident Evil Organ Transplant Popcorn Bag when you see Resident Evil at Regal. Tickets are on sale now: pic.twitter.com/x8J4grtVsk — Regal (@RegalMovies) September 1, 2026

Need a transplant? We recommend this popcorn bag 🫀🍿 Get your hands on the Resident Evil Organ Transplant Popcorn Bag when you see Resident Evil at Regal. Tickets are on sale now: pic.twitter.com/x8J4grtVsk

The popcorn bag reveal comes on the heels today of Sony’s release of a new poster for Resident Evil .

Weapons and Barbarian director Zach Cregger has been busy promoting Resident Evil with his main actor Austin Abrams. Cregger recently revealed that Abrams nearly died while they were shooting one particular zombie scene .

The filmmaker also conceded that he “took liberties” to make his movie better even though he knows Resident Evil 2, the game his film is inspired by, didn’t have snow or iPhones in it.

Cregger has also confirmed that his Resident Evil contains first-person sequences and that the games’ sinister Umbrella Corp. is indeed referenced in the film.

Hitting theaters on September 18, Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil is on track to have the biggest opening weekend of any movie in the Resident Evil film franchise .
